status: Reconstruction of the paper-described rule. Exact quantitative detector implementation not found in current public repository.
rule: Flag failure if any sliding-window Pearson(progress, time) < -0.5, unless success probability >= 0.5. Otherwise predict success.
paper_parameters: Success cutoff .5; correlation cutoff -.5 and window5 are documented example settings, window9 appears in one example. Full quantitative-table settings are not specified.
assumptions: Primary uses any-time success override; final-time override shown as sensitivity because the paper does not specify the time aggregation.
Our existing 19–24 event-augmented queries per episode; original failure-detector query cadence is unknown.
Undefined constant-window correlation produces no alarm; this rule cannot recognize a perfectly flat trace from correlation alone.
Cached native-model/collator batch1 SDPA BF16 inference reused; exact author runtime parity is not established.
metric: F1 and recalls with failure as positive. No continuous AUROC assigned to a binary rule.
repository_audit: ROBOMETER_REPOSITORY_AUDIT.md: six public branch tips and reachable history searched; dense inference clarified by authors in issue #16, full detector implementation not found.

dt_comparison.rule: Predict successful iff terminal expected DT <= distance_threshold.
dt_comparison.selection: Maximize development balanced accuracy; ties prefer fewer false successes then higher success-score threshold. Same established ABC calibration criterion.

comparison_caveat: DT threshold is development-calibrated; Robometer keeps paper-described example settings without ABC fitting. Same test episodes and failure-positive metrics, different decision rules.
